title: Cache granularity & low-bit tradeoffs — field notes
content:
Context: quick personal notes after skimming a few papers and running small local experiments. Goal is to capture hypotheses, short experiment plans, and items to surface in next eng-sync. Not a polished writeup — intentionally choppy.

Major takeaways so far:
- Cache granularity matters: storing prefixes at token-level vs chunk-level (e.g. 64-token chunks) trades storage+lookup overhead for eviction simplicity. For our workload (short convo bursts + occasional long docs) chunked caches reduce CPU overhead and lookup misses.
- Low-bit quantization interacts badly with KV caching entropy: compressed KV representations make collisions/approx errors more likely, which shows up as subtle degradation on factual recall when retrieving long-tail context.
- Prefetch heuristics (when using batching) can hide tail latency but can hurt freshness in highly interactive flows.

Notes & sketches:
1) Chunked-KV idea (64-token chunks)
  - store key/value per chunk, maintain chunk-to-original-range mapping
  - eviction policy: LRU at chunk granularity; prefer evicting oldest chunk parts of longest inactive context_id
  - quick pros/cons: fewer hash lookups, simpler alignment with quantized kernel boundaries; con: boundary artifacts when context split mid-sentence
2) Hybrid retention score
  - score = alpha * recency_norm + beta * token_importance (TF-IDF-ish on recent convo) + gamma * source_trust
  - tune alpha/beta/gamma per-customer profile; default: 0.6/0.3/0.1
  - for troubleshooting, log percentile of retained tokens vs evicted tokens

Experiments to run (local / small cluster):
- A) Chunk size sweep: [16, 32, 64, 128] tokens; measure mean lookup time, memory footprint, model perplexity on heldout QA prompts.
- B) Quantized KV ablation: FP16 baseline vs int8 vs 4-bit hybrid (GPTQ-style); measure factual answer accuracy on curated prompts (100 items), and measure similarity of retrieved KV vectors (cosine) to FP16 baseline.
- C) Prefetch aggressiveness: no prefetch / prefetch-if-latency>p50 / always-prefetch; measure tail p95 latency and mean freshness (defined as fraction of responses that depend on last 5 tokens).

Preliminary findings (scratch results):
- Chunk=64 seems like a pragmatic default: reduces lookup overhead ~18% vs 16-token, while maintaining negligible drop in QA accuracy on short-turn tests.
- int8 KV with symmetric per-channel quantization kept cosine similarity >0.94 for most keys, but failure modes concentrated on low-magnitude keys from seldom-used system prompts.
- aggressive prefetch reduced p95 by ~30ms on my dev rig for batch sizes >8, but increased stale-token incidents by ~2.5% on interactive traces.

Open questions and risks:
- Do we need different chunk sizes by model family (Llama2-style vs transformer variants)? Hypothesis: models with rotary/relative pos have less boundary confusion. Need to test.
- For private deployments with limited RAM, how do we surface graceful degradation — degrade to chunked LRU with smaller chunk size or fall back to no cache?
- Security: compressed KV blobs need integrity checks. If we accept compressed/int-bit blobs from other infra components, add CRC/HMAC.

Short config sketch (pseudocode):
- cache.chunk_size = 64
- cache.quantization = "int8_perchannel"
- cache.eviction_policy = "chunked_lru"
- cache.retention_weights = {"recency":0.6, "tfidf":0.3, "trust":0.1}

TODOs (short):
- [ ] Run chunk-size sweep on dataset X (deadline: 2028-05-07) — assign Mika
- [ ] Hook cosine-sim logging into tracing span for KV retrievals — assign me
- [ ] Draft short explainer for console team on cache chunking tradeoffs (1 page)

Quick links & reads I liked today:
- "Compression-aware KV caches" (arXiv) — notes: good math on quantization noise propagation
- Blog: "When caching meets low-bit inference" — practical heuristics, nice diagrams
- MLSys 2028 talk: "Latency knobs for interactive LLMs" — slides have a helpful p95 vs batch curve I want to reproduce

Notes to self (stream-of-consciousness):
- If we push chunk_size change we need migration strategy for existing cached blobs (compat header + on-access re-chunk).
- Consider exposing retention_weights as a per-route override in the API so apps can choose freshness vs cost.
- Record a quick demo of intentional staleness vs latency tradeoffs for sales folks — small GIFs show better than numbers.

Meeting bullets for next eng-sync:
- Present chunked-KV baseline findings (64 vs 16): perf + ML quality tradeoffs
- Proposal: default chunk=64 for hosted, allow per-deployment override for Private
- Risk mitigation: CRC + on-access re-quantization

End notes: keep this thin and iterative. Will turn into a fuller PRD if experiments show consistent wins.
